BIOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: BIOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemicals of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemicals of Life.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemicals of Life.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Chemicals of Life.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemicals of Life.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Nutri? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Nutri.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Nutri.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Nutri.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Nutri.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cell Structure and Specialisation? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cell Structure and Specialisation.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cell Structure and Specialisation.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cell Structure and Specialisation.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cell Structure and Specialisation.

5. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gaseous Exchange and Respiration? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Gaseous Exchange and Respiration.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gaseous Exchange and Respiration.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gaseous Exchange and Respiration.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gaseous Exchange and Respiration.

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

8. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Removing all vegetation

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.

10. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

11. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Milk souring

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Biology 1.2 Specimen Collection and Preservation 1.3 Cell Struct? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Biology 1.2 Specimen Collection and Preservation 1.3 Cell Struct.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Biology 1.2 Specimen Collection and Preservation 1.3 Cell Struct.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Biology 1.2 Specimen Collection and Preservation 1.3 Cell Struct.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Biology 1.2 Specimen Collection and Preservation 1.3 Cell Struct.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Transport? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Transport.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Transport.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Transport.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Transport.

16. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Chemicals of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Transport and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Nutri and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Gaseous Exchange and Respiration and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
